meta.title: Netfix: a network simulator in your browser
meta.description: Netfix is a free network simulator that runs in the browser: Cisco IOS command line, DHCP, Linux routers and servers, VPNs and ready-made labs. No install, no account. Open source under GPL-3.0.
nav.label: Main sections
hero.title: Practise networking in your browser, from the first cable to the firewall.
hero.lead: Netfix is a network simulator for classrooms and self-study. Wire up PCs, switches, routers and servers, configure them with a faithful Cisco IOS command line or a real Linux shell, and watch DHCP, DNS, NAT and VPNs work.
hero.note: Free and open source. Nothing to install and no account. Download it to use it offline.
hero.alt: Netfix workspace: a lab with a LAN, a DMZ and two Internet providers, with the firewall rules of the Linux router open beside it.
facts.label: Netfix at a glance
facts.1.text: installs or sign-ups: it opens in any modern browser
facts.2.text: ready-made labs, from basic DHCP to WireGuard
facts.3.text: automated tests checking the simulated behaviour
facts.4.text: free software: read it, change it, share it
problem.title: Network labs should not need a lab
problem.text: Real equipment is expensive and shared. Desktop simulators need installing, accounts and a particular operating system, and that is before the class has started. Students who want to practise at home often cannot.
solution.title: Netfix opens in a tab
solution.text: Send the link and everyone is working within seconds: on the classroom computers, on a laptop at home or on a tablet. Work is saved automatically in the browser and can be exported as a file to hand in or share.
features.title: What you can do with it
features.ios.title: A Cisco IOS command line that behaves like the real one
features.ios.text: User and privileged modes, abbreviations, the ? help, the ^ error marker and show output laid out as IOS 15 does. Configure interfaces, VLANs and trunks, DHCP pools and relays, ACLs, NAT and IPsec on the 2911 router and the 2960 switch.
features.ios.alt: Router command line showing show ip dhcp binding with three leases and show ip interface brief.
features.linux.title: Linux routers and servers with services you can inspect
features.linux.text: A bash 5.3 shell with nano and vim, nftables, sysctl, WireGuard and SSH. Servers provide DHCP, DNS, web and mail, each with a settings panel and a log, so you can see why a packet was dropped.
features.linux.alt: Linux router firewall panel with the forward chain rules for a LAN, a DMZ and the Internet.
features.touch.title: Made for tablets and phones too
features.touch.text: Terminals open full screen with a key bar for Esc, Tab, Ctrl and the arrows. Pinch to zoom the workspace, and draw coloured areas and labels to mark networks as you would on a whiteboard.
features.touch.alt: A PC Linux terminal on a phone: ip -br a and a successful ping to the gateway, with the touch key bar below.
features.more.title: Also included
features.more.1: Simulation mode that plays packets step by step, with the clock under your control
features.more.2: An emulated Internet with providers, public DNS and NAT
features.more.3: Built-in documentation and man pages for every command
features.more.4: Interface in British English and Spanish
labs.title: Labs ready to open
labs.lead: Each lab comes configured, with its networks marked and a short brief that says what to try.
labs.vlans: Router-on-a-stick with one pool per VLAN
labs.snooping: DHCP snooping against a rogue server
labs.servidores: Server with DHCP, DNS, web, mail and SSH
labs.internet: Two sites and public DNS over the Internet
labs.vpn-wireguard: WireGuard VPN with a branch behind NAT
labs.linux-dmz: Linux router with NAT and a DMZ
labs.dns-reenvio: Company DNS forwarding to the Internet
labs.bastionado: Hardening with ACLs, nftables and sshd
who.title: Who it is for
who.teachers.title: Teachers
who.teachers.text: Prepare a lab, save it as a file and share it. Everyone starts from the same network, whatever computer they have.
who.students.title: Students
who.students.text: Repeat the class exercises at home, break things without consequences and try commands before the exam.
who.self.title: Self-learners
who.self.text: Follow a certification syllabus or a course on your own, with documentation in the app to look things up as you go.
donate.title: Netfix is free. Keeping it that way depends on you.
donate.lead: If you would like to support this project so that it keeps improving and can cover its development costs, you can make a donation.
donate.why: Netfix has no adverts and no paid tier, and it never will. It is an independent project with no company behind it, so donations are the only income it has.
donate.funds.title: What your donation pays for
donate.funds.1: Development time for new devices, protocols and labs
donate.funds.2: Checking behaviour against real systems so the output stays faithful
donate.paypal: Payments are handled by PayPal. Netfix never sees your details.
donate.school: If Netfix saves your school or academy a licence, a donation from the department makes a real difference.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.free.a: Yes. Every feature is available to everyone with no limits. Donations are voluntary and unlock nothing extra.
faq.account.a: No. There is nothing to sign up for. Your work is kept in your own browser and never sent to a server.
faq.pt.q: Does it replace Cisco Packet Tracer?
faq.pt.a: It complements it. Netfix works where Packet Tracer cannot be installed, such as tablets and locked-down computers, and it adds Linux routers and servers. Netfix is an independent project and is not affiliated with Cisco.
faq.browsers.q: Which browsers does it work in?
faq.browsers.a: Current versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, on computers, tablets and phones.
faq.offline.q: Can I use it without an Internet connection?
faq.offline.a: Yes. Download the single-file version, netfix.html, and open it from your disk or a USB stick.
faq.licence.q: Can I change it or use it at my school?
faq.licence.a: Yes. Netfix is free software under the GNU GPL version 3 or later. You can use it anywhere, study the code and share your improvements under the same licence.
final.title: Your first network is one click away
final.text: Open Netfix, pick a lab and type enable.
